<STRUCT_0001>
Next, we show that this notion satisfies the conditions of
Sites, Definition <REF_0001>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> If <MATH_0002> is an isomorphism then <MATH_0003>
is a ph covering of <MATH_0004>.
<STRUCT_0003> If <MATH_0005> is a ph covering and for each
<MATH_0006> we have a ph covering <MATH_0007>, then
<MATH_0008> is a ph covering.
<STRUCT_0004> If <MATH_0009> is a ph covering
and <MATH_0010> is a morphism of schemes then
<MATH_0011> is a ph covering.
<STRUCT_0005>

Assertion (1) is clear.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Proof of (3). The base change <MATH_0001> is
locally of finite type by
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0001>.
hence we only need to check the condition on affine opens.
Let <MATH_0002> be an affine open subscheme.
Since <MATH_0003> is quasi-compact we can find a finite affine open
covering <MATH_0004> such that
<MATH_0005> maps into an affine open <MATH_0006>.
Choose a standard ph covering <MATH_0007>
refining <MATH_0008>.
By Lemma <REF_0002>
the base change <MATH_0009>
is a standard ph covering. Note that <MATH_0010>
is a standard ph covering as well.
By Lemma <REF_0003> 
the family <MATH_0011>
can be refined by a standard ph covering. Since
<MATH_0012> refines <MATH_0013>
we conclude.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Proof of (2). Composition preserves being locally of finite type,
see Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0004>.
Hence we only need to check the condition on affine opens.
Let <MATH_0014> be affine open. First we pick a standard ph covering
<MATH_0015> refining
<MATH_0016>.
Say the refinement is given by morphisms <MATH_0017> over <MATH_0018>.
Then
<MATH_0019>
is a ph covering by part (3). As <MATH_0020> is affine,
we can find a standard ph covering
<MATH_0021> refining this family.
Then we apply Lemma <REF_0005>
to see that <MATH_0022> can be refined by a
standard ph covering. Since <MATH_0023>
refines <MATH_0024> this finishes the proof.
